audit_findings.title: Common-unit value appears to ignore the GP incentive-distribution waterfall
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.352 million FY2025 and $19.351 million for nine months FY2026 theoretical LP dilution, equal to 14.1% and 16.7% of consolidated net income, respectively; valuation impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: OE attribution and shares: consolidated OE is divided by common and GP units as equal claims although the GP has disproportionate contractual participation rights
audit_findings.evidence: In any accounting period where the Company’s aggregate net income exceeds its aggregate distribution for such period, the Company is required to present net income per limited partner unit as if all of the earnings for the period were distributed, based on the terms of the Partnership agreement, regardless of whether those earnings would actually be distributed during a particular period from an economic or practical perspective.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated structural error, not merely a possibility. The equal-unit denominator does not reproduce the filed distribution waterfall. Because owner earnings represent distributable economic earnings, the GP claim survives even when earnings are retained. Filed allocations show a recurring claim large enough to materially reduce common-unit value, although the exact DCF reduction requires applying the waterfall to forecast cash flows.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild historical and forecast OE attributable to common units, apply the contractual waterfall to each forecast distribution, value common and GP claims separately, and confirm that management-plan compensation is deducted exactly once.

audit_findings.title: Positive growth may be credited without charging the acquisitions required to produce it
audit_findings.magnitude: $88.143 million FY2025 acquisition cash, 120.1% of the $73.4 million OE anchor; FY2023-FY2025 average acquisition cash was $52.441 million, 71.4% of the anchor; maintenance portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: OE and growth: acquisition cash is excluded from distributable OE while the base and bull cases credit 3% and 5% growth despite customer attrition
audit_findings.evidence: Accordingly, our ability to maintain or grow our customer base will depend on our ability to make acquisitions on economically acceptable terms.
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is demonstrated, although the necessary recurring acquisition charge is unresolved. SGU lost 4.7% of customers organically in FY2025 and states that acquisitions are needed to maintain or grow the customer base. Acquisition spending is comparable to or greater than normalized OE, so even a fraction classified as maintenance reinvestment could materially reduce sustainable OE and invalidate positive growth assumptions.
audit_findings.action: Separate acquisition spending into maintenance replacement and incremental growth components using acquired customers, retained customers, margins and purchase prices; deduct the maintenance component from OE and rerun all scenarios before applying positive growth.

audit_findings.title: The NETTI withdrawal obligation is a debt-like claim not represented by current earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.4 million recorded liability and $17.6 million filed fair value at June 30, 2026; $0.53 per diluted unit and 1.7% of $1.059 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity bridge: future withdrawal payments are not current OE expenses, but no corresponding liability is deducted from equity value
audit_findings.evidence: The withdrawal from the original employer pool triggered an undiscounted withdrawal obligation of $48.0 million that is to be paid in equal monthly installments over 30 years, or $1.6 million per year.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated, but its filed fair value is too small by itself to change the valuation conclusion. Deducting $17.6 million would reduce base value by about $0.53 per unit and the 30%-MOS buy-below level by about $0.37, versus the existing $9.62 gap between the $22.36 buy-below level and the $12.74 price.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the latest filed fair value from the equity bridge or explicitly include all scheduled payments in forecast OE, confirming that the original withdrawal charge is not counted twice.

audit_findings.title: Commodity derivative mark-to-market gains may contaminate normalized OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.977 million FY2023 charge, $19.018 million FY2024 charge and $13.390 million FY2025 credit; exact OE and anchor effects unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: OE and anchor growth: unrealized derivative gains or losses can enter annual net income and distort both individual OE observations and the fitted log trend
audit_findings.evidence: Therefore, we experience volatility in earnings as outstanding derivative instruments are marked-to-market and non-cash gains and losses are recorded prior to the sale of the commodity to the customer.
audit_findings.explanation: The mark-to-market amounts are demonstrated, but their inclusion in the supplied OE series is not established. Their signs reverse across years, so normalization could raise some OE years and lower others; the record therefore cannot establish the direction or materiality of the resulting trend-anchor change. The amounts are individually large relative to the $73.4 million anchor, so the issue cannot be dismissed.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every OE year to filed net income and cash flow, remove unrealized commodity-derivative movements, retain realized hedge effects exactly once with the underlying sales, and rerun the log-trend anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Other red-zone multiemployer plans create unrecognized contingent senior claims
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity bridge or future OE: a withdrawal, insolvency or mass-withdrawal assessment would create a senior cash claim beyond contributions already expensed
audit_findings.evidence: Accordingly, we could be assessed our share of unfunded liabilities should we terminate participation in these plans, or should there be a mass withdrawal from these plans, or if the plans become insolvent or otherwise terminate.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking contingent exposure rather than a demonstrated present valuation omission. The filings identify additional red-zone plans, but provide neither statutory withdrawal estimates nor probabilities. Existing contributions are already in earnings; only a future assessment would require a reserve or additional OE charge.
audit_findings.action: Obtain current statutory withdrawal-liability estimates for the IAM National Pension Fund, Teamsters Local 469 Pension Plan and Local 445 Pension Fund, assess triggering probabilities, and add a probability-weighted bridge reserve if supported.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 contains a nonrecurring property-sale gain that may remain in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.822 million pre-tax gain, 5.2% of the $73.4 million anchor; even a full dollar-for-dollar anchor reduction would lower base value by about $1.62 per unit and buy-below by about $1.14
audit_findings.mechanism: OE and trend anchor: a nonrecurring disposal gain may inflate FY2025 OE and the fitted normalized earning level while sale cash is separately represented in the bridge
audit_findings.evidence: Other income, net for fiscal 2025 of $3.8 million represents the net gain on the sale of land and building at a New Jersey operating location with a carrying value of $1.0 million for net cash proceeds of $4.8 million.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the gain remains in OE is unresolved, but its maximum plausible scale is not material to the conclusion. A conservative full $3.822 million reduction from the anchor would still leave an approximate buy-below level of $21.22, about $8.48 above the $12.74 market price; the actual trend effect should be smaller because FY2025 is only one of ten observations.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 OE to the filed income statement, remove the $3.822 million gain if present, confirm that sale proceeds are represented only through cash or reinvestment needs, and rerun the anchor.
